# 🏁 Milestone Project 3: Scientific Plotting Dashboard

In this milestone project, you will build an end-to-end telemetry and analysis dashboard for a mechanical damping experiment. Using NumPy, you will generate simulated physical responses, compute frequency spectra, simulate measurement noise, and produce a publication-grade, 4-panel dashboard with custom styling, legends, and annotations.

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  VIBRATION ANALYSIS DASHBOARD (4 PANELS)                 |
|                                                                          |
|  [ Panel 1: Time Domain Response ]     [ Panel 2: Phase Space Orbit ]    |
|  - Raw Displacements vs Time           - Velocity vs Position (x vs v)   |
|  - Theoretical Exponential Envelope    - Shows Orbital Decay Spiral      |
|                                                                          |
|  [ Panel 3: Measurement Error Dist ]   [ Panel 4: Energy Dissipation ]   |
|  - Sensor Noise Histogram              - Kinetic, Potential, and Total   |
|  - Expected Gaussian curve             - Mechanical energy decays        |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

## Complete Project Code: `vibration_dashboard.py`

Create a file named `vibration_dashboard.py` in Spyder and run it:

```python
"""
vibration_dashboard.py
======================
Milestone Project 3: 4-Panel Scientific Plotting Dashboard
for a Damped Harmonic Oscillator.
"""

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. Physics Parameters
m = 1.0        # Mass (kg)
k = 25.0       # Spring constant (N/m)
c = 0.6        # Damping coefficient (N*s/m)

# Derived natural frequency and damping ratio
omega_0 = np.sqrt(k / m)               # Natural freq = 5.0 rad/s
gamma = c / (2 * m)                    # Damping factor = 0.3
omega_d = np.sqrt(omega_0**2 - gamma**2) # Damped freq

# 2. Time Array & Trajectory Simulation
t = np.linspace(0, 15, 600)  # 15 seconds
envelope = np.exp(-gamma * t)
x_clean = envelope * np.cos(omega_d * t)
v_clean = -envelope * (gamma * np.cos(omega_d * t) + omega_d * np.sin(omega_d * t))

# Add realistic sensor noise (Gaussian)
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=2026)
noise = rng.normal(0, 0.05, size=len(t))
x_noisy = x_clean + noise

# Energy Calculations
ke = 0.5 * m * (v_clean ** 2)
pe = 0.5 * k * (x_clean ** 2)
total_energy = ke + pe

# 3. Build the 2x2 Dashboard Figure
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 8))
fig.suptitle("Damped Harmonic Oscillator Telemetry Dashboard", 
             fontsize=15, fontweight="bold", y=0.98)

# --- Panel 1: Time-Domain Position ---
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
ax1.plot(t, x_noisy, color="lightblue", alpha=0.7, label="Sensor Reading")
ax1.plot(t, x_clean, color="darkblue", linewidth=1.8, label="Analytic Model")
ax1.plot(t, envelope, "r--", linewidth=1.2, label="Decay Envelope")
ax1.plot(t, -envelope, "r--", linewidth=1.2)
ax1.set(title="Position vs Time", xlabel="Time (s)", ylabel="Displacement (m)")
ax1.grid(True, linestyle=":", alpha=0.6)
ax1.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=9)

# --- Panel 2: Phase Space Trajectory (Velocity vs Position) ---
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
ax2.plot(x_clean, v_clean, color="purple", linewidth=1.5)
ax2.plot(x_clean[0], v_clean[0], 'go', markersize=8, label="Start (t=0)")
ax2.plot(x_clean[-1], v_clean[-1], 'ro', markersize=6, label="End (t=15s)")
ax2.set(
    title="Phase Space (Orbital Decay)",
    xlabel="Position x (m)",
    ylabel="Velocity v (m/s)",
)
ax2.grid(True, linestyle=":", alpha=0.6)
ax2.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=9)

# --- Panel 3: Sensor Noise Distribution ---
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
counts, bins, _ = ax3.hist(
    noise, bins=25, density=True,
    color="teal", edgecolor="black", alpha=0.65,
)
# Overlay theoretical Gaussian curve
sigma = 0.05
gauss_x = np.linspace(-0.2, 0.2, 100)
gauss_y = (1 / (sigma * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5 * (gauss_x / sigma)**2)
ax3.plot(gauss_x, gauss_y, "r-", linewidth=2, label="Expected Gaussian")
ax3.set(
    title="Sensor Noise Residual Distribution",
    xlabel="Error (m)",
    ylabel="Probability Density",
)
ax3.grid(True, linestyle=":", alpha=0.6)
ax3.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=9)

# --- Panel 4: Mechanical Energy Dissipation ---
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
ax4.plot(t, total_energy, "k-", linewidth=2.0, label="Total Energy")
ax4.plot(t, ke, "b--", linewidth=1.2, label="Kinetic (KE)")
ax4.plot(t, pe, "g:", linewidth=1.2, label="Potential (PE)")
ax4.set(
    title="Energy Dissipation Over Time",
    xlabel="Time (s)",
    ylabel="Energy (Joules)",
)
ax4.grid(True, linestyle=":", alpha=0.6)
ax4.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=9)

# Tight layout and save figure
fig.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("vibration_dashboard.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
print("Dashboard generated successfully and saved to 'vibration_dashboard.png'!")
plt.show()
```

When run in Spyder, the complete multi-panel figure appears in the **Plots Pane** and a 300-DPI high-resolution PNG is saved to your project folder ready to embed in reports.
